name: AWS Route53
description: Protects against destructive AWS Route53 DNS operations like hosted zone deletion \ and record set DELETE changes.

destructive_patterns.name: route53-delete-hosted-zone
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 delete-hosted-zone permanently deletes a Route53 hosted zone.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a hosted zone removes ALL DNS records for that domain. Services, \ websites, and email that depend on these records will become unreachable. \ The zone must be empty (except NS/SOA) before AWS allows deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws route53 list-resource-record-sets to review records first \ - Export zone to file before deletion \ - Delete individual records instead of the entire zone

destructive_patterns.name: route53-change-resource-record-sets-delete
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets with DELETE removes DNS records.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DELETE actions in change-resource-record-sets immediately remove DNS records. \ DNS caching may provide brief respite, but resolvers will fail to reach your \ services once caches expire (often within minutes for low TTL records).

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use UPSERT action to modify rather than delete and recreate \ - Test changes in a non-production hosted zone first \ - Use aws route53 list-resource-record-sets to verify record state

destructive_patterns.name: route53-delete-health-check
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 delete-health-check permanently deletes a Route53 health check.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a health check can disrupt DNS failover. If records reference this \ health check, Route53 may route traffic to unhealthy endpoints or stop \ failover entirely, causing outages.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws route53 get-health-check to review configuration first \ - Check which records use this health check before deletion \ - Update dependent records to use a different health check first

destructive_patterns.name: route53-delete-query-logging-config
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 delete-query-logging-config removes a Route53 query logging configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting query logging stops DNS query visibility for that hosted zone. This \ can impact debugging, security monitoring, and compliance auditing. Historical \ logs in CloudWatch remain, but new queries will not be logged.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws route53 get-query-logging-config to review before deletion \ - Disable logging temporarily by updating the config instead \ - Ensure CloudWatch log retention meets compliance needs

destructive_patterns.name: route53-delete-traffic-policy
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 delete-traffic-policy permanently deletes a Route53 traffic policy.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a traffic policy removes the routing logic. Policy instances \ (applied to hosted zones) will fail to update or may stop working. This \ can disrupt geo-routing, latency-based routing, or weighted distributions.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - aws route53 list-traffic-policy-instances to check usage first \ - Create a new policy version instead of deleting \ - Delete policy instances before deleting the policy itself

destructive_patterns.name: route53-delete-reusable-delegation-set
destructive_patterns.description: aws route53 delete-reusable-delegation-set permanently deletes a reusable delegation set.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a reusable delegation set affects all hosted zones using it. If \ domain registrars point to these name servers, DNS resolution will fail \ for all associated domains until registrar records are updated.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Check which hosted zones use this delegation set first \ - Migrate zones to a different delegation set before deletion \ - Update domain registrar NS records after any changes
